question: Beshak, a festival celebrated on the full moon day of the lunar month Vaisakha, which falls in April or May, is a festival of which religion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Beshak** is a festival celebrated by Buddhists to commemorate the birth, enlightenment, and death of Gautama Buddha.
 
• This festival is observed on the full moon day of the lunar month Vaisakha, which usually falls in April or May.
 
• Beshak is one of the most significant festivals in Buddhism, with celebrations involving prayers, meditation, and various cultural activities.
 
• It is also known as **Vesak or Buddha Purnima** in different regions and is celebrated with great fervor in countries with significant Buddhist populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vaisakha**

 
 
• Vaisakha is the second month in the Hindu calendar, corresponding to April-May in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It is considered an auspicious month and is associated with various festivals and religious events in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Full Moon Day**
 
 
• The full moon day, known as Purnima in Sanskrit, is considered sacred in many cultures and religions.
 
• It marks the day when the moon is completely illuminated and is often associated with important religious observances and festivals.
 
 
 
• **Gautama Buddha**
 
 
• Gautama Buddha, also known as Siddhartha Gautama, was the founder of Buddhism.
 
• Born in Lumbini (modern-day Nepal) around the 5th century BCE, he attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, India.
 
• His teachings form the foundation of Buddhist philosophy, emphasizing the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
 
 
 
• **Vesak**
 
 
• Vesak, also known as Buddha Purnima or Buddha Jayanti, is a major Buddhist festival commemorating the birth, enlightenment, and death of Gautama Buddha.
 
• It is celebrated with various activities such as prayers, meditation, chanting, and cultural performances.
 
• Vesak is an occasion for Buddhists to reflect on the teachings of the Buddha and engage in acts of kindness and charity.
